concept: Why does the Moon always show us the same face?
title: The Locked Moon
tagline: It spins, yet never turns away.

science.hiddenLaw: Tidal locking by dissipative tidal torque: a deformable satellite's spin evolves due to tidal friction until its spin period equals its orbital period (1:1 spin-orbit synchronous rotation), the tidal bulge aligns with the primary, net torque goes to zero, and the same hemisphere continuously faces the primary.
science.plainStatement: Earth's gravity stretched the Moon into a slight bulge; flexing of that bulge created friction that slowed the Moon's spin until it now spins exactly once per orbit, so the same face always points toward Earth.
misconceptions: The Moon does not rotate or spin on its axis at all — it only orbits Earth.
The same face stays toward Earth because gravity holds the Moon motionless like a magnet, not because its spin is synchronized with its orbit.
The far side of the Moon is always dark and never gets sunlight (the permanent 'dark side').
Tidal locking is an instant coincidence or requires a perfectly circular orbit, not a gradual evolution driven by tidal dissipation.

sources.title: NASA Science - Tidal Locking and Why the Same Side of the Moon Faces Earth
Murray & Dermott - Solar System Dynamics: Tidal Evolution and Synchronous Rotation

story.mystery: Why does the Moon always show the same face while it still spins?
story.goal: Adjust spin, friction and orbit to reveal why the face never changes.

transfer.setup: A rocky exoplanet orbits a small star every 10 days. It starts spinning fast, its rock flexes with strong tides, and its orbit is slightly oval.
transfer.question: After a long time, how will the planet spin?
options: Once per orbit, same face to star
Not at all, frozen in place

checks.description: With tidal dissipation, spin period converges to orbital period (period_ratio ~1) regardless of fast initial spin
When locked, the angle between Moon's long axis and Earth direction stays near zero
Control: without tidal dissipation there is no synchronization - spin ratio stays at initial value
Disproves 'Moon doesn't spin' - even while same face points to Earth, spin rate is non-zero and equals orbital mean motion
Disproves 'far side always dark' - far side is sunlit about half the time when locked
